base_files.README.md:
# Synthetic receipts
The service records receipts in a local JSON ledger. A 200 paid response promises a receipt readable by a new file read; it is not a power-loss or fsync guarantee. Invalid requests return 400. Persistence errors return 503. Retrying an existing id with the same amount retains one receipt; conflicting amounts fail. One FileLedger instance serializes writes; cross-process locking is not implemented.
Local checks: node --test; node scripts/replay.mjs; node scripts/replay.mjs fail-write. Replays own and remove only temporary fixture directories.

base_files.README.md:
# Synthetic batch exports
The API functions are adapters called by a trusted caller. No HTTP listener, authentication integration, scheduler, or deployment definition is supplied. A successful request records a queued job and returns 202. An operator may invoke apps/worker/once.mjs with a storage directory and job id. The worker creates CSV and transitions the job. apps/web/export-view.mjs renders an API status object; it does not start or poll a worker.
FileJobs stores one JSON file per job and one CSV artifact. Only one worker per job is supported. There is no lock, retry scheduler, fsync contract, or failed-to-queued transition. Rows are synthetic names and integer cents, not real personal data. No retention or download-serving behavior is supplied.

base_files.README.md:
# Synthetic receipt applications
Order service, receipt worker, and operations view are separate application entry modules. No HTTP servers, deployed topology, daemon, or scheduler are configured. paths.sentFile is a local synthetic mail sink; it is not an SMTP service. paths.outbox is a local directory of messages. The one-worker fixture can consume pending messages and acknowledge after appending to the sink; no exactly-once delivery or crash-durability guarantee is declared. Inventory reservation is a synchronous validation stub, not a database write.
base_files.apps/operations/pending.mjs:
import { pending } from '../../packages/outbox/file-queue.mjs';
export async function receiptBacklog(paths) { return { pendingCount: (await pending(paths.outbox)).length }; }

import { appendFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
export async function sendReceipt(file, message) { await appendFile(file, JSON.stringify({ id: message.id, email: message.email }) + '\n'); }
